**Continuous 2.22.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.22.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.22.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.22.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.22.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.22.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.22.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.22.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.22.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.22.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.22.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.22.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.20.0

This release is about session storage. Chats are now saved as an append-only log: a save adds only what changed, a large tool output or image is stored once beside the chat, and a turn is saved while it runs, so if the window dies in the middle of a turn the chat reopens with it and offers Resume. **Clean up old sessions** removes the full prompts that releases before 2.20.0 stored in every session and in dev data, and the outputs a chat no longer uses. Local dev data keeps sizes and a hash of each prompt instead of its text, and an opt-in debug prompt log keeps the full prompts when you need them.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent. The new session format is on by default and can be turned off; the details are under Behaviour changes.

### Behaviour changes

- **Chats are saved in a new format, an append-only log.** A chat is now `sessions/<id>.jsonl`: each save appends only what changed instead of rewriting the whole chat file, and tool outputs over 4 KB, and any other text or image over 16 KB, are stored once in `sessions/<id>/blobs/`, so a tool output is no longer kept twice and a file read twice is stored once. In a measured 500-request agent session, the bytes written across all saves fell from 3.27 GB to 6.9 MB, and the chat on disk from 13.2 MB to 1.5 MB of log plus 5.4 MB of stored outputs. A chat saved the old way (`<id>.json`) is converted the next time it is saved, and the old file is removed only after the new one reads back the same; if it does not, the chat stays `.json` and a warning is logged. The extension, the terminal agent's `--resume`, `continuous clean` and the session list read both formats.
- **How to turn the new format off.** In Settings, open **Show Experimental Settings** and switch off **Save chats as an append-only log**. Chats are then written as `<id>.json` again, each one converted back as it is saved, and mid-turn saves stop. The terminal agent (`continuous`) still writes `.json` in this release, whatever the setting.
- **Local dev data no longer stores prompts and completions.** `dev_data/0.2.0/chatInteraction.jsonl` keeps `promptBytes`, `completionBytes`, `promptSha256` and the token counts of each chat request instead of its texts. A `data` destination you configured still receives the full event, as before.
- **The session size in the context meter counts stored outputs.** For a chat saved as a log, the line reads "Session 1.5 MB on disk (log and stored outputs), 812 items", and the 50 MB warning says that opening it reads all of it, rather than that every save rewrites it. Core's one-time warning past 50 MB counts the same total.

### New

- **A turn is saved while it runs.** Your message is saved when you send it, each tool result when the tool finishes, and the answer every few seconds (or 32 KB) as it streams. If the window or VS Code dies in the middle of a turn, the chat reopens with your message, the finished tool calls and their outputs, and the partial answer, and offers Resume. The webview now posts only what changed (`history/saveDelta`), so a save of a long chat no longer sends the whole chat to the extension host. This needs the append-only log, which is on by default.
- **Clean up old sessions.** **Continuous: Clean up old sessions** in the Command Palette, and `continuous sessions clean` in the terminal, report first and change nothing until you confirm (`--yes`, or the dialog in VS Code). They replace the full prompts that releases before 2.20.0 kept in every session with a short marker; reading each file in pieces, so a session too large to open is cleaned too. They also move out the stored outputs a log chat no longer refers to (an output whose message was edited or cut) and blob folders whose chat is gone, trim `dev_data` lines older than 90 days and drop the texts of kept `chatInteraction` lines, and move logs older than 14 days. Every rewritten file is checked before it replaces the original, and the originals go to `~/.continuous/cleanup-backups/<date>/`; `--delete-backups-older-than 30d`, or `continuous.sessionCleanup.deleteBackupsAfterDays` in VS Code, deletes old backup folders. A chat open in another window or agent, or written in the last 10 minutes, is left alone and reported, and so is an output the chat still refers to. After an update VS Code offers it once, and only when more than 100 MB can be reclaimed; **Don't ask again** is remembered. Flags: `--json`, `--dry-run`, `--no-dev-data`, `--no-logs`, `--dev-data-days`, `--logs-days`.
- **Debug prompt log**, off by default: the `continuous.debugPromptLog` setting in VS Code (application scope, so a workspace cannot turn it on), `--debug-prompt-log` or `CONTINUOUS_DEBUG_PROMPT_LOG=1` in the terminal. Each request's full prompt goes to `~/.continuous/logs/prompts/`, owner-only, with recognised secrets masked; five files share a 50 MB cap, the oldest is deleted first, and a file not written for 14 days is deleted.

### Fixes

- The cleanup leaves a chat that is mid-turn alone: every save to the log, including the saves made during a turn, records the chat as open in `~/.continuous/sessions-open/`, so a cleanup run from another window or the terminal skips it.

### Docs

- **Post-mortem and design** in `plans/research/prompt-logs-and-session-storage.md`: how prompt logs made sessions grow with the square of their length, and the storage plan (STOR rows) this release implements in part.
- **Storage and reset** (`docs/reference/storage-and-reset.mdx`): the `.jsonl` and `.json` session files and the blob folder, a new section on Clean up old sessions with a sample report, and the new `cleanup-backups/` and `sessions-open/` folders. The CLI reference documents `continuous sessions clean` and `--debug-prompt-log`, and the development data page what `chatInteraction` keeps.
- `PRIVACY.md` says what is stored locally now: sizes and a hash of each prompt, not its text.

### Upgrade notes

- **Going back to 2.20.0 or earlier.** Earlier versions do not read `.jsonl` chats, and their `continuous clean` does not age them out. Before you downgrade, switch off **Save chats as an append-only log** and open and send a message in each chat you want to keep, so it is saved as `.json` again.
- **The terminal agent writes `.json`.** It reads chats the extension saved as a log (`--resume`), but saves its own as `.json`, because `git-ai` reads the transcript path of the `.json` file.
- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
- **New folders in `~/.continuous`.** `sessions/<id>/blobs/` (stored outputs of a log chat), `sessions-open/` (which chats each running window or agent has open; safe to delete, it is rewritten) and `cleanup-backups/<date>/` (originals kept by Clean up old sessions; delete it to free the space).
- **Dev data consumers.** A tool that reads `prompt` or `completion` from local `chatInteraction.jsonl` now finds them absent; the config-yaml schema makes both optional and adds `promptBytes`, `completionBytes`, `promptSha256`, `promptTokens` and `completionTokens`.
